title: V2 Word Order & Satzklammer
subtitle: Master the signature German sentence bracket: finite verb in Position 2, infinitives & prefixes at the very end.

cheatSheet.summary: In German main clauses, the conjugated (finite) verb ALWAYS sits in Position 2. When you add a modal verb or separable verb, the second verb piece snaps to the very end—forming a bracket (Satzklammer) around the middle.
keyTakeaways: Position 1 (Vorfeld) holds ONE element: the subject, a time phrase ('Heute'), or a place ('In Berlin').
Position 2 (Linke Klammer) ALWAYS holds the conjugated verb—if Position 1 isn't the subject, the subject moves right behind the verb!
End Bracket (Rechte Klammer) holds infinitives (after können/müssen/wollen) or detached prefixes (an-, auf-, ein-, mit-).

patterns.translation: I have to get up early tomorrow.

cheatSheet.watchOut: Never put two elements before the verb! 'Heute ich gehe' is a classic English transfer error—it MUST be 'Heute gehe ich'.

exercises.instruction: Start with 'Heute' in Position 1—watch how the subject moves behind the verb!
exercises.rulePill: When 'Heute' takes Position 1, the finite verb 'lerne' MUST hold Position 2, pushing 'ich' into Position 3.

exercises.instruction: Form the modal verb Satzklammer (conjugated modal in Pos 2, infinitive at the end).
exercises.english: I have to work early tomorrow.
exercises.rulePill: Modal verb 'muss' opens the bracket in Position 2; the infinitive 'arbeiten' closes the bracket at the very end.

exercises.instruction: Split the separable verb 'anrufen' across the sentence bracket.
exercises.english: She is calling her brother right now.
exercises.fullGerman: Sie ruft jetzt ihren Bruder an.
exercises.rulePill: Separable verb 'anrufen' splits: stem 'ruft' sits in Position 2 while prefix 'an' snaps to the End Bracket.

exercises.subject: er / sie / es
exercises.english: Lisa can play the piano very well.
exercises.fullGerman: Lisa kann sehr gut Klavier spielen.
exercises.rulePill: In singular modal verbs, 'ich' and 'er/sie/es' are identical and take NO '-t' ending: ich kann, er/sie/es kann.

exercises.promptHint: Check the End Bracket verb form after a modal verb.
exercises.english: We want to go to the cinema on Saturday.
exercises.fullGerman: Wir wollen am Samstag ins Kino gehen.
exercises.rulePill: After modal verbs ('wollen'), the closing verb at the end MUST stay in the base infinitive ('gehen').

exercises.subject: er
exercises.prompt: Am Montag ___ er mit dem Zug nach Köln.
exercises.english: On Monday he travels to Cologne by train.
exercises.fullGerman: Am Montag fährt er mit dem Zug nach Köln.
exercises.rulePill: Strong verbs like 'fahren', 'schlafen', 'tragen' take an umlaut (a → ä) in du/er/sie/es: er fährt.

exercises.instruction: Build the question with the separable verb 'einkaufen'.
exercises.english: When are you going grocery shopping today?
exercises.rulePill: W-word ('Wann') occupies Position 1, finite verb ('kaufst') takes Position 2, and prefix 'ein' closes the sentence.

exercises.subject: sie (sg.)
exercises.english: In the evening she likes reading a crime novel.
exercises.fullGerman: Abends liest sie gern einen Krimi.
exercises.rulePill: 'lesen' shifts e → ie in du/er/sie/es: du liest, er/sie/es liest.

exercises.instruction: Start with the place phrase 'In Berlin' and keep the modal bracket intact.
exercises.english: In Berlin you can visit many museums.
exercises.fullGerman: In Berlin kann man viele Museen besuchen.
exercises.rulePill: 'In Berlin' fills Position 1 → 'kann' stays in Position 2 → 'besuchen' closes the End Bracket.
